# xdol

Extended Data Object Layers - dol-based tools

To install:	`pip install xdol`

[Documentation](https://i2mint.github.io/xdol/)

## Persistent memoizer (record/replay)

Wrap a costly function (a paid API, a slow render) so the first run records its result to disk and every later run replays it:

```python
from xdol import memoize_calls


@memoize_calls(
    store="tests/cassettes", mode="record"
)  # default mode is replay-only: a miss raises
def slow_square(x):
    return {"result": x * x}
```

Stable keys (`xdol.keys`), text / JSON / binary / paired `.json`+`.bin` codecs, any `MutableMapping` as the store (a folder, S3), spend-safe replay by default. See [misc/docs/persistent_memoizer.md]().

<p class="epythet-aggregates">This documentation as a single file: <a href="xdol.md">xdol.md</a> (Markdown, for agents).</p>


# _autosummary/xdol.access.html.md

# xdol.access

Persisted, mergeable per-key access statistics for any store.

An [`AccessLog`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog) is an append-only JSONL file of access events, folded into an
in-memory `{key: AccessStats}` on open; the log itself is a read-only `Mapping` of
key to (immutable) [`AccessStats`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessStats). [`track_access()`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.track_access) wraps any
`MutableMapping` so reads, writes and deletes are recorded. The log is the
`tracker` of [`xdol.tiering.TieredStore`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.TieredStore).

Filesystem atime cannot do this job (under `relatime` it is never a count, and any
backup pass resets it), hence an explicit log.

Event schema, one JSON object per line (plain string keys, so a filesystem tracer that
only knows paths can append to the same file, under the lock protocol below):

```default
{"k": key, "op": "read"|"write"|"delete"|"admit"|"release"|"pin"|"unpin",
 "n": bytes, "from": "hot"|"cold"|null, "ts": unix_seconds, "tag": str|null}
```

Only `k` and `op` are required: an event without `n` leaves the size alone.
Replay does not trust file order (several writers may append to one file): it parses
every line (a torn or ill-typed one, e.g. a NaN `ts` or a string `n`, is skipped),
applies the snapshot lines first, then folds the other events in `(ts, line number)`
order, exactly as live recording folds them. So a `delete` clears a key (pin
included) and only later-stamped events bring it back. An event without `ts` is
ordered right after the line before it in the file (it takes that line’s timestamp,
`0` at the top of the file): an unstamped `delete` still deletes what came before.

Folding a compacted prefix plus the events after it is exact when those events are
stamped after the compacted ones (the normal case). A *late* event, stamped before some
compacted events (a slow writer that stamped it, then waited for the lock while another
process compacted; or a clock running behind), folds only approximately: a snapshot
keeps no per-event history, so it cannot split its counts around a late, older
`delete`, nor order a late `pin`/`admit` against a compacted `unpin`/`release`.
Per-field stamps would fix the flag ordering; only a grace window (compacting events
older than some age, keeping the recent tail raw) fixes the counts, and only for events
less than that window late. Revisit (i2mint/xdol#44) if a multi-writer user shows the
drift matters.

Keys must be JSON scalars, in practice `str`: a key that does not survive a JSON
round trip (a tuple, a `Path`…) is counted in memory but lost or changed on reopen,
and recording one warns once.

A compacted file holds `{"k": key, "op": "snapshot", "stats": {...}}` lines, then one
`{"k": key, "op": "tombstone", "ts": t}` line per key ever deleted (its latest
delete, see [`AccessLog.tombstones`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog.tombstones)). Both are the baseline, folded before any
event and not counted as events; a tombstone only records the delete (it never removes
the key: the snapshot is already post-delete). Older readers skip tombstone lines.

A log built with `keep_tombstones_for=seconds` drops tombstones older than that at
compaction (default: keep them forever).

Compaction runs by default once the file holds more than `DFLT_COMPACT_ABOVE` events
(earlier versions never compacted on their own): it folds away the per-event history
(`tag`, `from`, each timestamp). Pass `compact_above=None` to keep the raw log.

Several processes may share one file. Every append, every replay and every compaction
holds an exclusive advisory lock (`flock`; `msvcrt.locking` on Windows) on a sidecar
of the real file (`<path>.lock`; beside the target of a symlink, a shortened hidden
name for names near the 255-byte limit: see `dol.FileLock`), and an appender checks,
under that lock, that its handle is still on the file at `path` (reopening it if
not), so compaction (which re-folds the file from disk, then replaces it) never drops
another writer’s events. An external appender (e.g. a filesystem tracer that only knows
paths) must do the same: from Python, `dol.LockedAppender(path, line_end=b"
")`;
otherwise hold `dol.file_lock(path)`’s lock around each append, opening `path`
afresh each time and writing each record as one \`\`
`-terminated write; or else every
log of that file must set ``compact_above=None`.

```pycon
>>> log = AccessLog()
>>> store = track_access({'a': b'xyz'}, tracker=log)
>>> store['a']
b'xyz'
>>> log['a'].reads
1
>>> 'a' in store  # membership is never recorded
True
>>> log['a'].frequency
1
```

### *class* xdol.access.AccessLog(path=None, \*, clock=<built-in function time>, tag=None, compact_above=100000, keep_tombstones_for=None)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

Append-only JSONL access log, readable as a `Mapping` of key -> AccessStats.

* **Parameters:**
  * **path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – log file; `None` keeps everything in memory (tests).
  * **clock** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – callable returning unix seconds.
  * **tag** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – label stamped on each event; defaults to `platform.node()`.
  * **compact_above** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – once the file holds more than this many events (lines other
    than snapshots), [`compact()`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog.compact) it: checked on open and as this log records
    (counting its own appends since then). `None`: never; the file then grows with
    every access.
  * **keep_tombstones_for** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – 

    seconds a delete’s tombstone is kept: [`compact()`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog.compact)
    drops those older than `clock() - keep_tombstones_for`, from the file and
    from this log’s memory. `None` (default): keep them forever, so a churning
    store’s tombstones grow without bound. A tombstone stops two things from
    resurrecting a deleted key: stats of another log merged by [`merge_stats()`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.merge_stats),
    and a late event of this file (see the module docstring) stamped before the
    delete. Keep them longer than any merged log can lag and any writer can be
    late; `0` drops them all at every compaction. Pruning happens only when
    [`compact()`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog.compact) runs (automatically only for a file log with `compact_above`
    > set). Retention is per file: whichever log compacts applies its own setting to
    > every writer’s tombstones, so let all logs sharing a file use the same one.

Opening replays the file in timestamp order (see the module docstring), so the
stats equal what recording those events live would give. Replay streams in constant
memory when the file is already in that order (the normal case for one writer) and
buffers it only when timestamps go back: a log several writers append to is out of
order, so opening it still costs memory proportional to its length (compaction
bounds that). Other writers’ events are seen on reopen, not live.

A tracker never raises into a store’s read path: if the file cannot be written,
a warning is issued once and counting continues in memory. Safe across processes,
forked ones included (see the module docstring); not thread-safe. A context
manager: leaving it closes the log’s files.

#### close()

Close the log’s files (it stays usable: it reopens them when needed).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### compact()

Rewrite the file as its folded state: snapshot lines, then tombstone lines.

Under the lock, so it re-folds the file from disk (keeping every writer’s
events, not only this log’s) and replaces it atomically; writers holding the
old file reopen the new one at their next append. This log’s in-memory stats
are left as they were; its tombstones older than `keep_tombstones_for` are
dropped, as from the file.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### record(key, op, nbytes=0, , served_from=None)

Record one `op` on `key` of `nbytes` bytes; raises `ValueError` on an unknown `op`, never on bad sizes.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### stats(key)

Alias of `self.get(key)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`AccessStats`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessStats) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### *property* tombstones *: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)*

Read-only `{key: timestamp of its latest delete}`, for [`merge_stats()`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.merge_stats).

Kept (and compacted) for every key ever deleted, re-created or not.

### xdol.access.default_access_log_for(store, \*\*kwargs)

An [`AccessLog`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog) beside `store`’s `rootdir` (never inside it).

Without a `rootdir`, an in-memory log, with a warning.

* **Return type:**
  [`AccessLog`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog)

### xdol.access.merge_stats(\*logs)

Merge several `Mapping[key, AccessStats]` (e.g. logs) into one dict.

Sums reads/writes, takes the `size` and `admitted_at` of the log with the
latest `last_access` (the one that saw the key’s current state), min
`first_seen` (ignoring unknown zeros), max `last_access`/`last_read`, OR of
`pinned`.

Deletes are honoured by timestamp: a log’s stats of a key whose latest event
(`first_seen`, `last_access` or `admitted_at`) is not after the latest delete
of that key in the *other* logs (their `tombstones`, when they have them) are left
out, as replaying all the logs as one would drop them. A log’s own tombstones never
apply to its own stats, which are post-delete already. Stats that span a delete and
a later re-creation count whole.

```pycon
>>> old = {'a': AccessStats(reads=3, last_access=5.0)}
>>> log = AccessLog(clock=lambda: 10.0)
>>> log.record('a', 'delete')
>>> 'a' in merge_stats(old, log)
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### xdol.access.track_access(store, , tracker=None, clock=None, tag=None)

Wrap `store` so reads, writes and deletes are recorded in `tracker`.

`__contains__`, `__iter__` and `__len__` are never recorded. Without a
`tracker`, [`default_access_log_for()`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.default_access_log_for) picks one, built with `clock` and
`tag` (passing either alongside a `tracker` is an error: set them on the
log). A value without `len` is recorded with size 0. The wrapped store is
available as `.store` and the log as `.tracker`.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### xdol.access.value_size(v)

`len(v)`, or `0` when `v` has no length (tracking never raises).

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)


# _autosummary/xdol.from_dol.html.md

# xdol.from_dol

Tools that left `dol`’s top-level namespace for xdol (dol issue #145).

`dol` keeps its core small. These names were exported at `dol`’s top level but used
nowhere inside dol, so their public home is now xdol: import them from here (or from
`xdol` directly). `dol.<name>` still works for one release, with a
`DeprecationWarning` pointing here.

`kvhead` and `ihead` are defined here. The others are, for now, re-exported from the
dol submodule that still defines them (so there is one definition of each); when dol
removes them, their definitions move into this module.

```pycon
>>> from xdol import kvhead, ihead, igroupby
>>> kvhead({'a': 1, 'b': 2})
('a', 1)
>>> ihead('abc', 2)
['a', 'b']
>>> dict(igroupby(['apple', 'avocado', 'banana'], key=lambda w: w[0]))
{'a': ['apple', 'avocado'], 'b': ['banana']}
```

### *class* xdol.from_dol.AttributeMutableMapping

Bases: `AttributeMapping`, [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

A mutable mapping that provides both attribute and dictionary-style access.

Extends AttributeMapping with mutation capabilities,
ensuring proper error handling and protocol compliance.

### Examples

```pycon
>>> ns = AttributeMutableMapping(apple=1, banana=2)
>>> ns.apple
1
>>> ns['banana']
2
>>> ns['cherry'] = 3
>>> ns.cherry
3
>>> list(ns)
['apple', 'banana', 'cherry']
>>> len(ns)
3
>>> 'apple' in ns
True
>>> del ns['banana']
>>> 'banana' in ns
False
```

A key mapper given as explicit `key_of_id`/`id_of_key` dicts (one is enough;
the other is derived, and both are checked to be inverse of each other).
Provides the `_key_of_id`/`_id_of_key` methods that `kv_wrap` looks for.

### *class* xdol.from_dol.SequenceKvReader(sequence, key=None, val=None, val_postproc=<class 'list'>)

Bases: `KvReader`

A KvReader that sources itself in an iterable of elements from which keys and values
will be extracted and grouped by key.

```pycon
>>> docs = [{'_id': 0, 's': 'a', 'n': 1},
...  {'_id': 1, 's': 'b', 'n': 2},
...  {'_id': 2, 's': 'b', 'n': 3}]
>>>
```

Out of the box, SequenceKvReader gives you enumerated integer indices as keys,
and the sequence items as is, as vals

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs)
>>> list(s)
[0, 1, 2]
>>> s[1]
{'_id': 1, 's': 'b', 'n': 2}
>>> assert s.get('not_a_key') is None
```

You can make it more interesting by specifying a val function to compute the vals
from the sequence elements

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs, val=lambda x: (x['_id'] + x['n']) * x['s'])
>>> assert list(s) == [0, 1, 2]  # as before
>>> list(s.values())
['a', 'bbb', 'bbbbb']
```

But where it becomes more useful is when you specify a key as well.
SequenceKvReader will then compute the keys with that function, group them,
and return as the value, the list of sequence elements that match that key.

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs,
...         key=lambda x: x['s'],
...         val=lambda x: {k: x[k] for k in x.keys() - {'s'}})
>>> assert list(s) == ['a', 'b']
>>> assert s['a'] == [{'_id': 0, 'n': 1}]
>>> assert s['b'] == [{'_id': 1, 'n': 2}, {'_id': 2, 'n': 3}]
```

The cannonical form of key and val is a function, but if you specify a str, int,
or iterable thereof,
SequenceKvReader will make an itemgetter function from it, for your convenience.

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs, key='_id')
>>> assert list(s) == [0, 1, 2]
>>> assert s[1] == [{'_id': 1, 's': 'b', 'n': 2}]
```

The `val_postproc` argument is `list` by default, but what if we don’t specify
any?
Well then you’ll get an unconsumed iterable of matches

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs, key='_id', val_postproc=None)
>>> assert isinstance(s[1], Iterable)
```

The `val_postproc` argument specifies what to apply to this iterable of matches.
For example, you can specify `val_postproc=next` to simply get the first matched
element:

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs, key='_id', val_postproc=next)
>>> assert list(s) == [0, 1, 2]
>>> assert s[1] == {'_id': 1, 's': 'b', 'n': 2}
```

We got the whole dict there. What if we just want we didn’t want the \_id, which is
used by the key, in our val?

```pycon
>>> from functools import partial
>>> all_but_s = partial(exclusive_subdict, exclude=['s'])
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs, key='_id', val=all_but_s, val_postproc=next)
>>> assert list(s) == [0, 1, 2]
>>> assert s[1] == {'_id': 1, 'n': 2}
```

Suppose we want to have the pair of (‘_id’, ‘n’) values as a key, and only ‘s’
as a value…

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs, key=('_id', 'n'), val='s', val_postproc=next)
>>> assert list(s) == [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3)]
>>> assert s[1, 2] == 'b'
```

But remember that using `val_postproc=next` will only give you the first match
as a val.

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs, key='s', val=all_but_s, val_postproc=next)
>>> assert list(s) == ['a', 'b']
>>> assert s['a'] == {'_id': 0, 'n': 1}
>>> assert s['b'] == {'_id': 1, 'n': 2}   # note that only the first match is returned.
```

If you do want to only grab the first match, but want to additionally assert
that there is no more than one,
you can specify this with `val_postproc=unique_element`:

```pycon
>>> s = SequenceKvReader(docs, key='s', val=all_but_s, val_postproc=unique_element)
>>> assert s['a'] == {'_id': 0, 'n': 1}
>>> # The following should raise an exception since there's more than one match
>>> s['b']
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
sources.NotUnique: iterator had more than one element
```

### xdol.from_dol.igroupby(items, key, val=None, group_factory=<class 'list'>, group_release_cond=<function <lambda>>, release_remainding=True, append_to_group_items=<method 'append' of 'list' objects>, grouper_mapping=<class 'collections.defaultdict'>)

The generator version of dol groupby.
Groups items according to group keys updated from those items through the given `key` function (mapping an item to its group key),
yielding the groups according to a logic defined by `group_release_cond`

* **Parameters:**
  * **items** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – iterable of items
  * **key** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`Hashable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Hashable)]) – The function that computes a key from an item. Needs to return a hashable.
  * **val** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – An optional function that computes a val from an item. If not given, the item itself will be taken.
  * **group_factory** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]) – The function to make new (empty) group objects and accumulate group items.
    group_items = group_collector() will be called to make a new empty group collection
    group_items.append(x) will be called to add x to that collection
    The default is `list`
  * **group_release_cond** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Hashable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Hashable), [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)], [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict), [`Hashable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Hashable), [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]]) – A boolean function that will be applied, at every iteration,
    to the accumulated items of the group that was just updated,
    and determines (if True) if the (group_key, group_items) should be yielded.
    The default is False, which results in
    `lambda group_key, group_items: False` being used.
  * **release_remainding** – Once the input items have been consumed, there may still be some
    items in the grouping “cache”. `release_remainding` is a boolean that indicates whether
    the contents of this cache should be released or not.
* **Yields:**
  `(group_key, items_in_that_group)` pairs

The following will group numbers according to their parity (0 for even, 1 for odd),
releasing a list of numbers collected when that list reaches length 3:

```pycon
>>> g = igroupby(items=range(11),
...             key=lambda x: x % 2,
...             group_release_cond=lambda k, v: len(v) == 3)
>>> list(g)
[(0, [0, 2, 4]), (1, [1, 3, 5]), (0, [6, 8, 10]), (1, [7, 9])]
```

If we specify `release_remainding=False` though, we won’t get

```pycon
>>> g = igroupby(items=range(11),
...             key=lambda x: x % 2,
...             group_release_cond=lambda k, v: len(v) == 3,
...             release_remainding=False)
>>> list(g)
[(0, [0, 2, 4]), (1, [1, 3, 5]), (0, [6, 8, 10])]
```

# >>> grps = partial(igroupby, group_release_cond=False, release_remainding=True)

Below we show that, with the default `group_release_cond = lambda k, v: False`
and release_remainding=True\`\` we have `dict(igroupby(...)) == groupby(...)`

```pycon
>>> from functools import partial
>>> from dol import groupby
>>>
>>> kws = dict(items=range(11), key=lambda x: x % 3)
>>> assert (dict(igroupby(**kws)) == groupby(**kws)
...         == {0: [0, 3, 6, 9], 1: [1, 4, 7, 10], 2: [2, 5, 8]})
>>>
>>> tokens = ['the', 'fox', 'is', 'in', 'a', 'box']
>>> kws = dict(items=tokens, key=len)
>>> assert (dict(igroupby(**kws)) == groupby(**kws)
...         == {3: ['the', 'fox', 'box'], 2: ['is', 'in'], 1: ['a']})
>>>
>>> key_map = {1: 'one', 2: 'two'}
>>> kws.update(key=lambda x: key_map.get(len(x), 'more'))
>>> assert (dict(igroupby(**kws)) == groupby(**kws)
...         == {'more': ['the', 'fox', 'box'], 'two': ['is', 'in'], 'one': ['a']})
>>>
>>> stopwords = {'the', 'in', 'a', 'on'}
>>> kws.update(key=lambda w: w in stopwords)
>>> assert (dict(igroupby(**kws)) == groupby(**kws)
...         == {True: ['the', 'in', 'a'], False: ['fox', 'is', 'box']})
>>> kws.update(key=lambda w: ['words', 'stopwords'][int(w in stopwords)])
>>> assert (dict(igroupby(**kws)) == groupby(**kws)
...         == {'stopwords': ['the', 'in', 'a'], 'words': ['fox', 'is', 'box']})
```

### xdol.from_dol.ihead(store, n=1)

Get the first item of an iterable, or a list of the first n items

```pycon
>>> ihead(iter('abc'))
'a'
>>> ihead(iter('')) is None
True
```

### xdol.from_dol.kvhead(store, n=1)

Get the first item of a kv store, or a list of the first n items

```pycon
>>> kvhead({'a': 1, 'b': 2}, 5)
[('a', 1), ('b', 2)]
>>> kvhead({}) is None
True
```

### xdol.from_dol.mk_store_from_path_format_store_cls(store=None, \*, subpath='', store_cls_kwargs=None, key_type=<function namedtuple>, keymap=<class 'dol.naming.StrTupleDict'>, keymap_kwargs=None, name=None, \_\_module_\_=None, \_\_name_\_=None, \_\_qualname_\_=None, \_\_doc_\_=None, \_\_annotations_\_=None, \_\_defaults_\_=None, \_\_kwdefaults_\_=None)

Wrap a store (instance or class) that uses string keys to make it into a store that uses a specific key format.

* **Parameters:**
  * **store** – The instance or class to wrap
  * **subpath** – The subpath (defining the subset of the data pointed at by the URI
  * **store_cls_kwargs** – # if store is a class, the kwargs that you would have given the store_cls to make itself
  * **key_type** – The key type you want to interface with: `dict`, `tuple`,
    `namedtuple`, `str`, or one of those names as a string
  * **keymap** – # the keymap instance or class you want to use to map keys
  * **keymap_kwargs** – # if keymap is a cls, the kwargs to give it (besides the subpath)
  * **name** – The name to give the class the function will make here
* **Returns:**
  An instance of a wrapped class

### Example

```python
# Get a (session, bt) indexed LocalJsonStore
s = mk_store_from_path_format_store_cls(LocalJsonStore,
                                               os.path.join(root_dir, 'd'),
                                               subpath='{session}/d/{bt}',
                                               keymap_kwargs=dict(process_info_dict={'session': int, 'bt': int}))
```

### xdol.from_dol.redirect_getattr_to_getitem(cls=None, , keys_have_priority_over_attributes=False, \_\_module_\_=None, \_\_name_\_=None, \_\_qualname_\_=None, \_\_doc_\_=None, \_\_annotations_\_=None, \_\_defaults_\_=None, \_\_kwdefaults_\_=None)

A mapping decorator that redirects attribute access to \_\_getitem_\_.

#### WARNING
This decorator will make your class un-pickleable.

* **Parameters:**
  **keys_have_priority_over_attributes** – If True, keys will have priority over existing attributes.

```pycon
>>> @redirect_getattr_to_getitem
... class MyDict(dict):
...     pass
>>> d = MyDict(a=1, b=2)
>>> d.a
1
>>> d.b
2
>>> list(d)
['a', 'b']
```

### xdol.from_dol.regroupby(items, \*key_funcs, \*\*named_key_funcs)

Recursive groupby. Applies the groupby function recursively, using a sequence of key functions.

#### NOTE
The named_key_funcs argument names don’t have any external effect.

They just give a name to the key function, for code reading clarity purposes.

#### SEE ALSO
groupby, itertools.groupby, and dol.source.SequenceKvReader

```pycon
>>> # group by how big the number is, then by it's mod 3 value
>>> # note that named_key_funcs argument names doesn't have any external effect (but give a name to the function)
>>> regroupby([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], lambda x: 'big' if x > 5 else 'small', mod3=lambda x: x % 3)
{'small': {1: [1, 4], 2: [2, 5], 0: [3]}, 'big': {0: [6], 1: [7]}}
>>>
>>> tokens = ['the', 'fox', 'is', 'in', 'a', 'box']
>>> stopwords = {'the', 'in', 'a', 'on'}
>>> word_category = lambda x: 'stopwords' if x in stopwords else 'words'
>>> regroupby(tokens, word_category, len)
{'stopwords': {3: ['the'], 2: ['in'], 1: ['a']}, 'words': {3: ['fox', 'box'], 2: ['is']}}
>>> regroupby(tokens, len, word_category)
{3: {'stopwords': ['the'], 'words': ['fox', 'box']}, 2: {'words': ['is'], 'stopwords': ['in']}, 1: {'stopwords': ['a']}}
```

### xdol.from_dol.to_zip_file(b, zip_filepath, filename=None, , compression=8, allow_overwrites=True, pwd=None, encoding='utf-8')

Zip input bytes and save to a single-file zip file.

* **Parameters:**
  * **b** ([`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Input bytes or string
  * **zip_filepath** – zip filepath to save the zipped input to
  * **filename** – The name/path of the zip entry we want to save to
  * **encoding** – In case the input is str, the encoding to use to convert to bytes

### xdol.from_dol.trace_getitem(store, k, layer_attrs=('store',))

A generator of layered steps to inspect a store.

* **Parameters:**
  * **store** – An instance that has the base.Store interface
  * **k** – A key
  * **layer_attrs** – The attribute names that should be checked to get the next layer.
* **Returns:**
  A generator of (layer, method, value)

We start with a small dict:

```pycon
>>> d = {'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'}
```

Now let’s add layers to it. For example, with wrap_kvs:

```pycon
>>> from dol.trans import wrap_kvs
```

Say that we want the interface to not see the `'.num'` strings, and deal with numerical values, not strings.

```pycon
>>> s = wrap_kvs(d,
...              key_decoder=lambda x: x[:-len('.num')],
...              key_encoder=lambda x: x + '.num',
...              value_decoder=lambda x: int(x),
...              value_encoder=lambda x: str(x)
...             )
>>>
```

Oh, and we want the interface to display upper case keys.

```pycon
>>> ss = wrap_kvs(s,
...              key_decoder=lambda x: x.upper(),
...              key_encoder=lambda x: x.lower(),
...             )
```

And we want the numerical unit to be the kilo (that’s 1000):

```pycon
>>> sss = wrap_kvs(ss,
...                value_decoder=lambda x: x / 1000,
...                value_encoder=lambda x: x * 1000
...               )
>>>
>>> dict(sss.items())
{'A': 1.0, 'B': 2.0}
```

Well, if we had bugs, we’d like to inspect the various layers, and how they transform the data.

```python
# Here's how to do that:

# >>> for layer, method, value in trace_getitem(sss, 'A'):
# ...     print(layer, method, value)
# ...
# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
# NameError: name 'trace_getitem' is not defined
```

```pycon
>>> from dol.dig import trace_getitem
>>>
>>> for layer, method, value in trace_getitem(sss, 'A'):
...     print(layer, method, value)
...
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _id_of_key A
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _id_of_key A
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _id_of_key a
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _id_of_key a
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _id_of_key a.num
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _id_of_key a.num
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} __getitem__ 1000
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _obj_of_data 1000
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _obj_of_data 1000
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _obj_of_data 1000
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _obj_of_data 1000
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _obj_of_data 1000
{'a.num': '1000', 'b.num': '2000'} _obj_of_data 1.0
```

# _autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md

# xdol.keys

Robust, stable cache keys: turn a call’s inputs into a short, filesystem-safe string.

A persistent cache (see [`xdol.memoize`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#module-xdol.memoize)) is only as good as its keys. A key must be

- **stable across runs and machines** – never derived from a memory address, set
  iteration order or dict insertion order;
- **insensitive to superficial differences** – dict key order, surrounding whitespace;
- **loud about what it cannot make stable** – an object whose only description is
  `<Foo object at 0x7f...>` would give a *different key every run* (a cache that
  never hits, or, in replay-only mode, a spurious miss), so it raises
  [`UnstableKeyError`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.UnstableKeyError) instead of silently hashing the address.

```pycon
>>> robust_key({"b": 1, "a": 2}, prompt="  hi ") == robust_key({"a": 2, "b": 1}, prompt="hi")
True
>>> len(robust_key(1, 2, x=3))
32
```

Keys are a **stability contract**: committed caches (e.g. cassette directories) are keyed
by these hashes, so the output for JSON-able inputs does not change between releases.

Customize with [`make_key_func()`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.make_key_func) – drop non-semantic arguments (callbacks, loggers),
bind to the wrapped function’s signature, pick the digest, or teach it your own types
with a `__cache_key__` method.

```pycon
>>> def f(prompt, *, logger=None, retries=3): ...
>>> key = make_key_func(f, drop=["logger", "retries"])
>>> key("hi", logger=print) == key(prompt="hi", retries=9)
True
```

### Functions

| [`hash_payload`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.hash_payload)(payload, \*[, digest, length])      | Hash an already-normalized JSON-able `payload` to a short hex string.              |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_key_func`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.make_key_func)([func, drop, apply_defaults, ...]) | Build a key function `(*args, **kwargs) -> str`, customized.                       |
| [`normalize`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.normalize)(obj, \*[, collapse_whitespace, ...])   | Recursively reduce `obj` to a JSON-able structure that is equal for equal meaning. |
| [`robust_key`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.robust_key)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)                   | The default key function: a stable SHA-256 (32 hex chars) of the normalized call.  |

### Exceptions

| [`UnstableKeyError`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.UnstableKeyError)   | An input has no run-stable description, so no stable key can be made from it.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *exception* xdol.keys.UnstableKeyError

Bases: [`TypeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError)

An input has no run-stable description, so no stable key can be made from it.

Fix it by giving the object a `__cache_key__()` method, dropping the argument from
the key (`make_key_func(f, drop=[...])`), or passing `on_unstable="ignore"` if
you accept a key that may change between runs.

### xdol.keys.hash_payload(payload, , digest='sha256', length=32)

Hash an already-normalized JSON-able `payload` to a short hex string.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### xdol.keys.make_key_func(func=None, , drop=(), apply_defaults=False, collapse_whitespace=False, on_unstable='raise', digest='sha256', length=32, prefix='')

Build a key function `(*args, **kwargs) -> str`, customized.

* **Parameters:**
  * **func** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – if given, calls are bound to its signature first, so `f(1, 2)`,
    `f(1, b=2)` and `f(a=1, b=2)` share a key. Required for `drop`.
  * **drop** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – names of parameters of `func` to leave out of the key – the
    non-semantic ones (callbacks, loggers, timeouts, `self`).
  * **apply_defaults** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – with `func`, also hash default values, so `f(x)` equals
    `f(x, y=<default>)`. Off by default: adding a defaulted parameter later
    then does not invalidate existing caches (changing a default does not
    either – turn this on if that matters to you).
  * **collapse_whitespace** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – see [`normalize()`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.normalize).
  * **on_unstable** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'raise'`, `'warn'`, `'ignore'`]) – see [`normalize()`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.normalize).
  * **digest** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – hash algorithm (any [`hashlib`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/hashlib.html#module-hashlib) name) and key length in hex chars.
  * **length** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – hash algorithm (any [`hashlib`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/hashlib.html#module-hashlib) name) and key length in hex chars.
  * **prefix** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – prepended to every key (e.g. a namespace or version: `"v2-"`).
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

With no arguments this is [`robust_key()`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.robust_key).

```pycon
>>> make_key_func()("x") == robust_key("x")
True
>>> def f(a, b=1, *, log=None): ...
>>> k = make_key_func(f, drop=["log"], apply_defaults=True)
>>> k(1) == k(1, 1) == k(a=1, log=print)
True
```

### xdol.keys.normalize(obj, , collapse_whitespace=False, on_unstable='raise')

Recursively reduce `obj` to a JSON-able structure that is equal for equal meaning.

- strings are stripped (and, with `collapse_whitespace`, inner runs of whitespace
  become one space – off by default since whitespace can be meaningful in code or
  markdown);
- mappings get string keys, sorted; lists and tuples become lists;
- sets are sorted; bytes are replaced by their digest; paths, enums, dates,
  dataclasses, numpy-like arrays and callables get a tagged, stable description;
- an object with a `__cache_key__()` method is described by what it returns;
- pandas objects are described by their full content; bound methods by function and
  instance; lambdas raise (indistinguishable);
- anything else falls back to `repr`, vetted by `on_unstable` (see
  [`UnstableKeyError`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.UnstableKeyError)). A `repr` can still be lossy (truncated, or leaving out
  > state): for such types define `__cache_key__`.

Limitation: recursion costs ~2 frames per nesting level, so structures nested deeper
than ~400 levels raise `RecursionError`.

```pycon
>>> normalize({"b": " x ", "a": (1, 2)})
{'a': [1, 2], 'b': 'x'}
>>> normalize({3, 1, 2})
{'__set__': [1, 2, 3]}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### xdol.keys.robust_key(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

The default key function: a stable SHA-256 (32 hex chars) of the normalized call.

Calls whose arguments are semantically equal – same values up to dict key order and
surrounding whitespace – get the same key.

```pycon
>>> robust_key("a", n=1) == robust_key("a ", n=1)
True
>>> robust_key("a", n=1) == robust_key("a", n=2)
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md

# xdol.memoize

Persistent memoization with record/replay modes, for costly calls.

A transparent wrapper that persists a function’s results in a `MutableMapping` keyed by
a stable hash of the call. It is a VCR cassette for *any* function, not just HTTP: the
first run records, every later run replays from the store – no call, no cost, no network.
The driving use is tests of code that calls paid APIs (LLMs, image/video generation),
which must stay free and fast, but it serves any expensive, deterministic-enough call.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> calls = []
>>> @memoize_calls(store=tempfile.mkdtemp(), mode="record")
... def slow_square(x):
...     calls.append(x)
...     return {"result": x * x}
>>> slow_square(3), slow_square(3)
({'result': 9}, {'result': 9})
>>> calls
[3]
```

**Replay is the default; recording is an opt-in.** Under the default `mode=None` a call
whose key is not in the store raises [`CacheMiss`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.CacheMiss) instead of calling the function,
unless the run sets the `XDOL_MEMOIZE_RECORD` environment variable (see
[`recording_enabled()`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.recording_enabled)). A key that quietly moved would otherwise read as a normal,
billable test run. Spending is an act that carries a flag. For a plain memoizer that
records on a miss, pass `mode="record"` (as above).

Four pieces, each a keyword argument with a good default (a *seam*):

- `key_func` – input to key; default [`xdol.keys.robust_key()`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.robust_key) (see also `drop=`);
- `codec` – result to bytes; `"json"` (default), `"text"`, `"bytes"` for binary
  assets, or `"paired"` for a `(metadata, asset_bytes)` result stored as
  `<key>.json` + `<key>.bin` (see [`xdol.x_codecs`](_autosummary/xdol.x_codecs.html.md#module-xdol.x_codecs));
- `store` – a directory path (a stable, committable folder: see
  [`file_cache_store()`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.file_cache_store)), or any `MutableMapping`. Pass a bytes store such as
  > `s3dol.s3_store(bucket)` and the codec is applied on top, so swapping the filesystem
  > for S3 changes nothing at the call site;
- `mode` – `"replay"`, `"record"`, `"refresh"` or `"off"`; see `MODES`.

**Cache the top-level composite**: wrap the whole `prompt -> JSON -> asset URL ->
downloaded bytes` pipeline, not each intermediate API step, so one intent maps to one
final result. Nothing enforces this; it keeps the surface area (and the number of
cassettes to review) small.

The wrapper preserves the function’s signature and metadata (`functools.wraps`) and
supports coroutine functions. Exceptions raised by the function are never cached.

### Module Attributes

| [`RECORD_ENV`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.RECORD_ENV)          | Set to a truthy value to let `mode=None` calls record on a miss.                                                                                                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TRUTHY_ENV_VALUES`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.TRUTHY_ENV_VALUES)   | Environment-variable spellings that count as "on".                                                                                                                     |
| [`DFLT_CORRUPT_ERRORS`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.DFLT_CORRUPT_ERRORS) | Errors that mean "this stored entry cannot be decoded" (as opposed to a store/network failure, which must never be mistaken for a missing entry and cost a real call). |

### Functions

| [`file_cache_store`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.file_cache_store)(rootdir, \*[, codec])            | A persistent, atomic, codec-aware `MutableMapping` over a directory.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`memoize_calls`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.memoize_calls)([func, codec, key_func, drop, ...]) | Persistently memoize `func` into `store` (record/replay).              |
| [`recording_enabled`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.recording_enabled)([env])                          | True when the environment variable `env` is set to a truthy value.     |

### Classes

| [`AtomicFiles`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.AtomicFiles)(\*args[, delete_func])   | A bytes store over a directory whose writes are atomic.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|

### Exceptions

| [`CacheCorrupt`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.CacheCorrupt)                     | A stored entry exists but cannot be decoded (replay mode refuses to guess).       |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CacheMiss`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.CacheMiss)                        | A memoized call missed its store while recording was disabled.                    |
| [`CacheWriteError`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.CacheWriteError)(message, result) | The function ran but its result could not be stored (e.g. not JSON-serializable). |

### *class* xdol.memoize.AtomicFiles(\*args, delete_func=<built-in function remove>, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: `Files`

A bytes store over a directory whose writes are atomic.

Plain file writes can leave a truncated cassette if the process dies mid-write, which
then fails to decode (or worse, decodes). Here each value is written to a temporary
sibling and renamed into place (`os.replace`), and temporary files are invisible to
iteration (dol’s hidden `.name.<random>.tmp` siblings; leftovers of the older
`*.xdol-tmp` scheme are skipped too). Missing sub-directories of a key (`"a/b"`) are created.

### *exception* xdol.memoize.CacheCorrupt

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

A stored entry exists but cannot be decoded (replay mode refuses to guess).

### *exception* xdol.memoize.CacheMiss

Bases: [`LookupError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#LookupError)

A memoized call missed its store while recording was disabled.

The alternative to this exception is a real, possibly billable call nobody asked
for. Two things cause it: an input the store has genuinely never seen, and a cache
**key** that moved under an unchanged input – usually because the key was computed
over something incidental (a rendered global registry, a timestamp, a path).

### *exception* xdol.memoize.CacheWriteError(message, result)

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

The function ran but its result could not be stored (e.g. not JSON-serializable).

The result is not lost: it is the `result` attribute.

### xdol.memoize.DFLT_CORRUPT_ERRORS *= (<class 'xdol.x_codecs.CodecDecodeError'>,)*

Errors that mean “this stored entry cannot be decoded” (as opposed to a store/network
failure, which must never be mistaken for a missing entry and cost a real call).

### xdol.memoize.RECORD_ENV *= 'XDOL_MEMOIZE_RECORD'*

Set to a truthy value to let `mode=None` calls record on a miss.

### xdol.memoize.TRUTHY_ENV_VALUES *= frozenset({'1', 'on', 'true', 'yes'})*

Environment-variable spellings that count as “on”.

### xdol.memoize.file_cache_store(rootdir, , codec='json')

A persistent, atomic, codec-aware `MutableMapping` over a directory.

Keys are filenames, values are decoded objects. `rootdir` is
created if missing and is meant to be a stable folder you commit (a cassette
directory), not a temp dir. `codec="paired"` stores `(metadata, asset_bytes)`
values as `<key>.json` + `<key>.bin`.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> store = file_cache_store(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> store["k"] = {"a": 1}
>>> store["k"], list(store)
({'a': 1}, ['k'])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### xdol.memoize.memoize_calls(func=None, \*, store, codec=None, key_func=None, drop=(), mode=None, default_mode='replay', record_env='XDOL_MEMOIZE_RECORD', corrupt_errors=(<class 'xdol.x_codecs.CodecDecodeError'>, ), on_write_error='raise', copy_results=None, reread_after_write=True, miss_hint='')

Persistently memoize `func` into `store` (record/replay).

Usable as `memoize_calls(fn, store=...)` or as a decorator
`@memoize_calls(store=...)`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **func** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the (costly) function; wrap the *composite* top-level call.
  * **store** – a directory path (-> [`file_cache_store()`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.file_cache_store)), or a `MutableMapping`.
  * **codec** – `None` (default) means a path gets `"json"` and a mapping is used as
    it is (its values are the results). Otherwise `store` is a *bytes* mapping
    and this is applied on top: `"json"`, `"text"`, `"bytes"`,
    `"paired"`, a [`xdol.x_codecs.Codec`](_autosummary/xdol.x_codecs.html.md#xdol.x_codecs.Codec), or an `(encode, decode)` pair.
  * **key_func** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – input to key. Default [`xdol.keys.robust_key()`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.robust_key).
  * **drop** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – parameter names of `func` to leave out of the key (callbacks, loggers,
    `self`); builds the key with [`xdol.keys.make_key_func()`](_autosummary/xdol.keys.html.md#xdol.keys.make_key_func), which also
    binds calls to the signature. Not combinable with `key_func`.
  * **mode** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'replay'`, `'record'`, `'refresh'`, `'off'`], [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[], [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'replay'`, `'record'`, `'refresh'`, `'off'`]], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]) – one of `MODES`, a zero-argument callable returning one (evaluated on
    every call), or `None` (default) for: `"record"` if the `record_env`
    variable is truthy, else `default_mode`. Read at call time, so setting the
    variable after import (e.g. in a pytest hook) works.
  * **default_mode** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'replay'`, `'record'`, `'refresh'`, `'off'`]) – what `mode=None` means when the environment does not opt in.
    `"replay"` (default) makes spending an explicit act.
  * **record_env** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – name of the opt-in environment variable.
  * **corrupt_errors** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`type`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)[[`BaseException`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#BaseException)], [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]) – exception types raised by reading an entry that mean “undecodable”
    (default: [`xdol.x_codecs.CodecDecodeError`](_autosummary/xdol.x_codecs.html.md#xdol.x_codecs.CodecDecodeError), which the codecs raise;
    add your own for an object-valued store that can fail to load). In replay
    mode they raise [`CacheCorrupt`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.CacheCorrupt); when recording, the entry is recomputed
    and overwritten, with a warning. Any other error – a network failure, a
    misconfigured store – propagates and never costs a real call.
  * **copy_results** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – deep-copy values read from the store, so callers cannot mutate the
    cache. `None` (default) means: yes when `store` is an object-valued
    mapping used as is (a codec makes a fresh object per read anyway).
  * **reread_after_write** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – after recording, return the value as read back from the store,
    so a recording run and a replay run return *the same thing* (JSON turns tuples
    into lists and int keys into strings). Turn off to skip the extra read of a
    large asset.
  * **on_write_error** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'raise'`, `'warn'`]) – what to do if a fresh result cannot be stored: `"raise"`
    [`CacheWriteError`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.CacheWriteError) (carrying the result) or `"warn"` and return it.
  * **miss_hint** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – text appended, on its own line, to the [`CacheMiss`](_autosummary/xdol.memoize.html.md#xdol.memoize.CacheMiss) message:
    how *your* suite records (`"Record with: pytest --record-cassettes"`) and
    what recording costs, which the generic advice cannot know.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)

The returned wrapper has attributes `cache_store`, `key_func`, `cache_key(\*args,
\*\*kwargs)` and `cache_mode()` (the mode that would apply now).

Known limitations:

- On a method, `obj.method.cache_key(...)` is unbound (`self` is not supplied
  for you): call `Cls.method.cache_key(obj, ...)`, also when using `drop=['self']`.
- There is no cross-process lock: concurrent recorders of one key may each call the
  function (the last write wins; entries are written atomically, so none is torn).

### xdol.memoize.recording_enabled(env='XDOL_MEMOIZE_RECORD')

True when the environment variable `env` is set to a truthy value.

The opt-in is environment-level rather than per-call, so “this run may spend” is one
visible fact about the run instead of a property of each test.

```pycon
>>> recording_enabled("XDOL_SURELY_UNSET_VARIABLE")
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)


# _autosummary/xdol.paths.html.md

# xdol.paths

Tools for manipulating paths.

A path is a sequence of objects that represent a reference or location.
Often paths are strings that use a special character (e.g. ‘/’) to distinguish the
separate objects in the sequence.

### Functions

| [`extract_path_segments`](_autosummary/xdol.paths.html.md#xdol.paths.extract_path_segments)(path, \*[, sep, depth, ...])   | Extracts the first `depth` segments of a path, delimited by `sep`.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### xdol.paths.extract_path_segments(path, , sep='/', depth=1, trailing_sep=True)

Extracts the first `depth` segments of a path, delimited by `sep`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **path** – The path to extract the segments from.
  * **sep** – The delimiter to use to separate the segments.
  * **depth** – The number of segments to extract.
  * **trailing_sep** – Whether to add a trailing delimiter to the result.
* **Returns:**
  The first `depth` segments of the path, delimited by `sep`.

By default, the function will use depth=1 and the system’s path separator as `sep`.

```pycon
>>> extract_path_segments("snap/crackle/pop/cereal", sep='/')
'snap/'
```

You can specify a different `depth`.

```pycon
>>> extract_path_segments("snap/crackle/pop/cereal", depth=2, sep='/')
'snap/crackle/'
```

Note that if the path starts with the `sep` delimiter, the result will be different.

```pycon
>>> extract_path_segments("/snap/crackle/pop/cereal", depth=2, sep='/')
'/snap/'
```

If `path` is not a string, the function will assume it’s an iterable of strings,
and return an iterable of the results.

```pycon
>>> list(extract_path_segments(
...     ['a.file', 'a/folder', 'a/folder_with/subfolders/', 'another/folder'],
...     depth=2, sep='/'
... ))
['a.file', 'a/folder', 'a/folder_with/', 'another/folder']
```

You can of course specify a different delimiter.

```pycon
>>> extract_path_segments("snap.crackle.pop.cereal", sep='.', depth=2)
'snap.crackle.'
```

That last dot doesn’t make sense here? Tell the function to not add the separator
at the end of the result.

```pycon
>>> extract_path_segments(
...     "snap.crackle.pop.cereal", sep='.', depth=2, trailing_sep=False
... )
'snap.crackle'
```

### *class* xdol.pystores.PyFilesReader(store=<class 'dict'>)

Bases: `PrefixRelativizationMixin`, `Store`

Mapping interface to .py files of a folder.
Keys are relative .py paths.
Values are the string contents of the .py file.

Important Note: If the byte contents of the .py file can’t be decoded (with a simple bytes.decode()),
an empty string will be returned as it’s value (i.e. contents).

```pycon
>>> import asyncio
>>> s = PyFilesReader(asyncio)
>>> assert len(s) > 10  # to test length (currently asyncio has 29 modules
>>> 'locks.py' in s
True
```

But you can also specify an \_\_init_\_.py filepath or the directory containing it.

```pycon
>>> import os
>>> init_filepath = asyncio.__file__
>>> dirpath_to_asyncio_modules = os.path.dirname(init_filepath)
>>> ss = PyFilesReader(init_filepath)
>>> sss = PyFilesReader(dirpath_to_asyncio_modules)
>>> assert list(s) == list(ss) == list(sss)
```

# _autosummary/xdol.registry.html.md

# xdol.registry

A typed dict-backed plugin registry.

The [`Registry`](_autosummary/xdol.registry.html.md#xdol.registry.Registry) is the dict-pattern that recurs across packages
(`falaw.registry`, `lacing.processors`, `lookbook.registry`, …): a
dict, a `register(key, value)` call, a `get(key)` lookup, an iteration
protocol, and a small number of conveniences that each package keeps
re-implementing — aliases, lazy loading, decorator-form registration, and
conflict policies. `Registry` collects these into one builtin-only,
`MutableMapping`-compatible class.

Basic use:

```pycon
>>> from xdol.registry import Registry
>>> tools = Registry[str](name="tools")
>>> tools.register("hello", "say hi")
'say hi'
>>> tools["hello"]
'say hi'
>>> sorted(tools)
['hello']
```

Decorator form:

```pycon
>>> handlers = Registry()
>>> @handlers.register_decorator("greet")
... def greet(name): return f"hi {name}"
>>> handlers["greet"]("ada")
'hi ada'
```

Aliases:

```pycon
>>> models = Registry()
>>> models.register("fal-ai/flux/dev", {"family": "flux"})
{'family': 'flux'}
>>> models.alias("flux", "fal-ai/flux/dev")
>>> models["flux"]
{'family': 'flux'}
>>> "flux" in models
True
```

Conflict policies — `error` (default), `replace`, `keep`:

```pycon
>>> r = Registry(on_conflict="error")
>>> r.register("k", 1)
1
>>> r.register("k", 2)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
xdol.registry.RegistryConflict: 'k' is already registered in <Registry>
```

```pycon
>>> r2 = Registry(on_conflict="keep")
>>> r2.register("k", 1)
1
>>> r2.register("k", 2)  # silently kept
1
>>> r2["k"]
1
```

Plain assignment replaces; opt in to `strict_setitem` to make it honour the policy:

```pycon
>>> loose = Registry()
>>> loose["k"] = 1
>>> loose["k"] = 2  # explicit assignment replaces
>>> loose["k"]
2
>>> strict = Registry(strict_setitem=True)
>>> strict["k"] = 1
>>> strict["k"] = 2
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
xdol.registry.RegistryConflict: 'k' is already registered in <Registry>
```

Lazy loading — value is built on first access:

```pycon
>>> calls = []
>>> def make_thing():
...     calls.append(1)
...     return {"built": True}
>>> r3 = Registry()
>>> r3.register_lazy("thing", make_thing)
>>> calls
[]
>>> r3["thing"]
{'built': True}
>>> r3["thing"]  # cached after first build
{'built': True}
>>> calls
[1]
```

Subscription — observe registrations as they happen:

```pycon
>>> r4 = Registry()
>>> seen = []
>>> sub = r4.subscribe(lambda key, value: seen.append((key, value)))
>>> r4.register("a", 1)
1
>>> r4.register("b", 2)
2
>>> seen
[('a', 1), ('b', 2)]
>>> sub.unsubscribe()
>>> r4.register("c", 3)
3
>>> seen  # no longer notified
[('a', 1), ('b', 2)]
```

#### register(key, value, , tags=())

Register `value` under `key`. Returns `value` so it can be used inline.

If `key` is an alias, it is resolved to its canonical key first, so the

Call `callback(key, value)` on every eager registration.

Lazy registrations do NOT fire the callback at registration time;
only when the value is materialized via `__getitem__`. This
keeps subscribers free of partially-built state.

# _autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md

# xdol.tiering

A bounded hot store over a cold source of truth (write-through, GDSF release).

`TieredStore(hot, cold, budget_bytes=...)` is a `MutableMapping`: writes go to
`cold` first, then `hot`; reads are served from `hot` when present, else from
`cold` (and admitted to `hot` when the policy says so). Placement is decided by a
[`PlacementPolicy`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.PlacementPolicy) (default [`GdsfPolicy`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.GdsfPolicy): Greedy-Dual-Size-Frequency with
aging, Cherkasova 1998) from the statistics of an [`xdol.access.AccessLog`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog), whose
clock is the store’s clock.

Verbs are free functions, store first: [`sweep()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.sweep), [`pin()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.pin), [`unpin()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.unpin),
[`status()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.status), [`prefetch()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.prefetch), [`local_paths()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.local_paths).

Values must support `len` (their size in bytes): `__setitem__` raises `TypeError`
before writing anything otherwise. A value read from `cold` without `len` counts
as size 0. Single-threaded: there is no locking.

```pycon
>>> hot, cold = {}, {}
>>> store = TieredStore(hot, cold, budget_bytes=None, tracker=AccessLog())
>>> store['a'] = b'hello'
>>> cold['a'], hot['a']
(b'hello', b'hello')
>>> status(store)['hot_bytes']
5
```

### *class* xdol.tiering.GdsfPolicy(, high_watermark=0.85, low_watermark=0.75, min_residency_s=604800, admit_after_reads=2, admit_window_s=2592000, cost_per_request=1.0, cost_per_byte=0.0, seed_half_life_s=2592000)

Bases: `_ResidencyPolicy`

Greedy-Dual-Size-Frequency with aging, plus pins, minimum residency and
second-hit admission.

Each hot key carries `H = L + F * cost(size) / size`, fixed when it is accessed,
with `F` its accesses since admission to hot, `cost(size) = cost_per_request +
cost_per_byte * size` and `L` the H of the last released key at that time
(per process; resets at restart). Releasing the lowest H raises `L`, so a key
not accessed for a while loses to newer ones however often it was read. A key
already hot when this process first sees it starts fresh, `F = 1`, as if just
admitted: its logged history (often long, all of it older than `L`’s reset)
would otherwise keep it favoured after every restart. A key not accessed during
this process (a cron `sweep`) is ranked on its recency instead: `F` is
`0.5 ** (age / seed_half_life_s)`, `age` being the time since its
`last_access`, so among such keys of equal size the least recently used goes first (a key seeded this way and then accessed continues from `F + 1`).

#### on_hot_access(key, stats, , admitted)

Bump the key frequency (a first-seen key starts fresh) and record its size.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### on_hot_drop(key)

Forget the key.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### priority(frequency, size)

H of a key accessed now with this frequency and size.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### *class* xdol.tiering.TieredStore(hot, cold, , budget_bytes, policy=None, tracker=None, max_item_fraction=1.0)

Bases: [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

Bounded hot store over a cold source of truth. See the module docstring.

* **Parameters:**
  * **budget_bytes** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – 

    `None`: hot is a full mirror (never released, every read miss
    admitted); `0`: cold-only, no hot tier (writes skip hot and read misses are not admitted, but only
    [`sweep()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.sweep) enforces it: [`prefetch()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.prefetch) and [`local_paths()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.local_paths) still fill
    > hot until the next sweep, which releases every hot copy, protected or not);
    > `> 0`: bounded.
  * **policy** ([`PlacementPolicy`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.PlacementPolicy) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – a [`PlacementPolicy`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.PlacementPolicy); default [`GdsfPolicy`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.GdsfPolicy).
  * **tracker** ([`AccessLog`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.AccessLog) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an `AccessLog` (its `clock` is the store’s clock); default
    [`xdol.access.default_access_log_for()`](_autosummary/xdol.access.html.md#xdol.access.default_access_log_for) `(hot)`.
  * **max_item_fraction** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – in `(0, 1]`; with a bounded budget, an item larger than
    `max_item_fraction * budget_bytes` is never held hot by the store itself: a
    read miss is served from cold without admission, and a write goes to cold only
    (dropping any stale hot copy). The default `1.0` keeps only items larger than
    the whole budget out. [`prefetch()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.prefetch) and [`local_paths()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.local_paths) are explicit
    requests and are exempt.

Keys already in `hot` at construction are not recorded as accesses. Their size
comes from the tracker, else from the file size when `hot` is file-backed, else
counts as 0 until the key’s next hot hit.

### xdol.tiering.local_paths(store, , path_of=None)

Read-only `{key: real file path}`; materialises each key into `hot`.

Materialisation is an explicit request, like [`prefetch()`](_autosummary/xdol.tiering.html.md#xdol.tiering.prefetch): exempt from the
policy and from `max_item_fraction`.

`path_of(key)` gives the file path of `key` in `hot`; the default is
`dol.path_of()` on the hot store, which follows wrapped layers (`TypeError` on access if `hot` is not
file-backed, before anything is fetched; `KeyError` for a key leaving its root).
`FileNotFoundError` is raised if the file is not there after materialisation.
`key in paths` checks the store without fetching.

# _autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md

# xdol.updating

Controlled updates of one mapping from another, with customizable policies.

`update_with_policy` decides, key by key, whether to copy a source item into a
target mapping. It goes beyond `dict.update()` with:

- built-in policies (always update, update if different, prefer target, prefer source, an alias of always update)
- custom decision functions and custom “key info” extractors (compare sizes,
  hashes or timestamps instead of reading values)
- statistics about what was examined, updated, added, unchanged or deleted
- specialized entry points (content-hash comparison, timestamps, local files)

A last section names the operations on a master / copy pair (companions of
`xdol.tiering`): `backfill` (push to master what only the copy has),
`reconcile` (update the copy from master) and `verify` (compare without
writing).

Custom update logic with a hash function:

```pycon
>>> target = {"a": "hello", "b": "world"}
>>> source = {"a": "hello!", "c": "python"}
>>> update_by_content_hash(target, source, hash_function=lambda x: len(x))
{'examined': 2, 'updated': 1, 'added': 1, 'unchanged': 0, 'deleted': 0}
>>> target
{'a': 'hello!', 'b': 'world', 'c': 'python'}
```

Using convenience methods:

```pycon
>>> update_with_policy.missing_only(target, source)
{'examined': 2, 'updated': 0, 'added': 0, 'unchanged': 2, 'deleted': 0}
>>> target
{'a': 'hello!', 'b': 'world', 'c': 'python'}
```

### xdol.updating.add_as_attribute_of(obj, name=None)

Decorator to add the function as an attribute of the object.

* **Parameters:**
  * **obj** – The object to which the function will be added
  * **name** – The name of the attribute to be added, if None, uses the function name
* **Returns:**

### Examples

```pycon
>>> def foo():
...     return "bar"
...
>>> @add_as_attribute_of(foo)
... def baz():
...     return "qux"
...
>>> foo.baz()
'qux'
```

### xdol.updating.backfill(\*, master, copy, keys_to_consider=<function \_copy_keys>)

Push to `master` the items that only `copy` has. Never overwrites.

Decisions use key presence only: the one value read is `copy[k]` for each key
actually pushed, so nothing is ever downloaded from a cold (e.g. S3) master.
`keys_to_consider`: keys, or `(master, copy) -> keys` (default: copy’s keys).
Each key is tested with `in` on both stores: where that is a request (e.g. S3),
wrap the store as `dol.trans.cached_keys(store, keys_cache=set)` to list it once
and test membership against that listing, kept current on writes (it must be
`set`: a `list` cache re-lists the store on every write).

```pycon
>>> master, copy = {'a': 1}, {'a': 9, 'b': 2}
>>> backfill(copy=copy, master=master).added
1
>>> master
{'a': 1, 'b': 2}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`UpdateStats`](_autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md#xdol.updating.UpdateStats)

### xdol.updating.content_hash_key_info(store)

A `key_info_for`: `key -> content hash` for `store`.

Text and bytes-like values give a sha256 of their content, tagged by kind so
that `'a'` and `b'a'` differ. Any other value is returned as is. Hashes
compare exactly as the values do with `==` (`1 == 1.0`, dict order ignored),
so this is for when a hash, not the value, is what must be kept or sent.

```pycon
>>> h = lambda v: content_hash_key_info({'k': v})('k')
>>> h(b'a') == h(bytearray(b'a')), h(b'a') == h('a')
(True, False)
>>> h({'x': 1})
{'x': 1}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`KeyInfoExtractor`](_autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md#xdol.updating.KeyInfoExtractor)

### xdol.updating.local_file_timestamp(store, key)

Get the modified timestamp of a file in a local file store.

Uses inner_most_key to handle relative paths correctly, resolving to
the full path before getting the timestamp.

* **Parameters:**
  * **store** – A mapping whose keys resolve to file paths
  * **key** – A key in the store
* **Returns:**
  The modification timestamp of the file
* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### xdol.updating.reconcile(\*, master, copy, key_info_for=None, policy=DefaultPolicy.UPDATE_IF_DIFFERENT, keys_to_consider=<function \_just_source_keys>)

Update `copy` from `master`: what differs is rewritten, unless `policy`
says otherwise.

* **Parameters:**
  * **key_info_for** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)], [`KeyInfoExtractor`](_autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md#xdol.updating.KeyInfoExtractor)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `key_info_for(store)` gives the `key -> info` compared for
    that store (e.g. sizes or ETags, to avoid reading values); default: the values
    themselves, any pair that can’t be compared counting as different (and, for a
    policy that looks at presence only, nothing is read to decide).
  * **policy** ([`DefaultPolicy`](_autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md#xdol.updating.DefaultPolicy) | [`UpdateDecider`](_autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md#xdol.updating.UpdateDecider)) – a [`DefaultPolicy`](_autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md#xdol.updating.DefaultPolicy), or a custom decider, which gets
    [`MISSING`](_autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md#xdol.updating.MISSING) as the info of a key absent from a store.
  * **keys_to_consider** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[`K`], [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping), [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[`K`]]]) – keys, or `(master, copy) -> keys` (default: master’s).
* **Return type:**
  [`UpdateStats`](_autosummary/xdol.updating.html.md#xdol.updating.UpdateStats)

Each key is tested with `in` on both stores: where that is a request (e.g. S3),
wrap the store as `dol.trans.cached_keys(store, keys_cache=set)` to list it once
and test membership against that listing, kept current on writes (it must be
`set`: a `list` cache re-lists the store on every write).

```pycon
>>> master, copy = {'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 3}, {'a': 9, 'c': 3}
>>> s = reconcile(master=master, copy=copy)
>>> s.updated, s.added, s.unchanged
(1, 1, 1)
>>> copy
{'a': 1, 'c': 3, 'b': 2}
```

### xdol.updating.union_iter(\*iterables)

Generator yielding unique hashable items from an iterable of iterables.

* **Parameters:**
  **iterables** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[`T`]) – An iterable where each element is itself an iterable of hashable items.
* **Yields:**
  `T` – Unique items from the nested iterables, in order of first appearance.
* **Return type:**
  [*Generator*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Generator)[*T*, *None*, *None*]

### Example

```pycon
>>> list(union_iter(['a', 'b'], ['b', 'c']))
['a', 'b', 'c']
>>> list(union_iter({'a': 1, 'b': 2}.keys(), {'b': 3, 'c': 4}.values()))
['a', 'b', 3, 4]
```
